claim: Histone acetylation regulates chromatin structure and gene expression.
source: Histone acetylation regulates chromatin structure and gene expression and is removed by histone deacetylases (HDACs).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by extensive literature and scientific consensus.

claim: Histone acetylation is removed by histone deacetylases (HDACs).
source: Histone acetylation regulates chromatin structure and gene expression and is removed by histone deacetylases (HDACs).
evidence: This is a fundamental concept in epigenetics, supported by scientific consensus.

claim: HDACs are commonly found in various protein complexes to confer distinct cellular functions.
source: HDACs are commonly found in various protein complexes to confer distinct cellular functions, but how the multi-subunit complexes influence deacetylase activities and site-selectivities in chromatin is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in the field and is referenced throughout the manuscript.

claim: How multi-subunit HDAC complexes influence deacetylase activities and site-selectivities in chromatin is poorly understood.
source: HDACs are commonly found in various protein complexes to confer distinct cellular functions, but how the multi-subunit complexes influence deacetylase activities and site-selectivities in chromatin is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement establishes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: The CoREST complex shows a notable preference for deacetylation of histone H3 acetyl-Lys9 vs. acetyl-Lys14.
source: Previously we reported the results of studies on the HDAC1 containing CoREST complex and acetylated nucleosome substrates which revealed a notable preference for deacetylation of histone H3 acetyl-Lys9 vs. acetyl-Lys14 (Wu et al, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Wu et al, 2018).

claim: Five class I HDAC complexes (CoREST, NuRD, Sin3B, MiDAC and SMRT) show a wide variety of deacetylase rates in a site-selective manner.
source: Here we analyze the enzymatic properties of five class I HDAC complexes: CoREST, NuRD, Sin3B, MiDAC and SMRT with site-specific acetylated nucleosome substrates. Our results demonstrate that these HDAC complexes show a wide variety of deacetylase rates in a site-selective manner.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A Gly13 in the histone H3 tail is responsible for a sharp reduction in deacetylase activity of the CoREST complex for H3K14ac.
source: A Gly13 in the histone H3 tail is responsible for a sharp reduction in deacetylase activity of the CoREST complex for H3K14ac.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from mutant nucleosome studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: Reversible histone acetylation regulates gene expression, DNA replication, cell growth, and differentiation.
source: Reversible histone acetylation (Cole, 2008) regulates a range of major fundamental biological processes including gene expression, DNA replication, cell growth, and differentiation (Jamaladdin et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Histone acetyltransferases (HATs) catalyze Lys sidechain acetylation on the N-terminal tails of each of the four core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, and H4).
source: Histone acetyltransferases (HATs) catalyze Lys sidechain acetylation on the N-terminal tails of each of the four core histones (Weinert et al., 2018), H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 that comprise nucleosomes, the building blocks of chromatin (Helin and Dhanak, 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Nucleosomes are the building blocks of chromatin.
source: Histone acetyltransferases (HATs) catalyze Lys sidechain acetylation on the N-terminal tails of each of the four core histones (Weinert et al., 2018), H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 that comprise nucleosomes, the building blocks of chromatin (Helin and Dhanak, 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a fundamental concept in chromatin biology, supported by citation.

claim: Particular HATs such as p300/CBP, PCAF/GCN5, and Myst family members display varying degrees of site selectivity in the context of histone tail peptides and/or chromatin.
source: Enzymological and cellular analysis has shown that particular HATs such as p300/CBP, PCAF/GCN5, and Myst family members display varying degrees of site selectivity in the context of histone tail peptides and/or chromatin (Shortt et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: p300/CBP is best known to acetylate Lys18 and Lys27 in histone H3.
source: For example, p300/CBP is best known to acetylate Lys18 and Lys27 in histone H3 (Dancy and Cole, 2015), whereas PCAF/GCN5 prefers to acetylate Lys14 and Lys9 of histone H3 (Ali et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PCAF/GCN5 prefers to acetylate Lys14 and Lys9 of histone H3.
source: For example, p300/CBP is best known to acetylate Lys18 and Lys27 in histone H3 (Dancy and Cole, 2015), whereas PCAF/GCN5 prefers to acetylate Lys14 and Lys9 of histone H3 (Ali et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) remove acetyl-Lys modifications in chromatin and other proteins.
source: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) remove acetyl-Lys modifications in chromatin and other proteins and belong to two major families in humans (Taunton et al., 1996), classical HDACs which include 11 Zn metallohydrolase enzymes and seven sirtuins (Wang et al., 2017), that catalyze NAD-dependent Lys deacetylation (Falkenberg and Johnstone, 2014).
evidence: This is a fundamental concept supported by citations.

claim: HDACs belong to two major families in humans: classical HDACs which include 11 Zn metallohydrolase enzymes and seven sirtuins.
source: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) remove acetyl-Lys modifications in chromatin and other proteins and belong to two major families in humans (Taunton et al., 1996), classical HDACs which include 11 Zn metallohydrolase enzymes and seven sirtuins (Wang et al., 2017), that catalyze NAD-dependent Lys deacetylation (Falkenberg and Johnstone, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Sirtuins catalyze NAD-dependent Lys deacetylation.
source: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) remove acetyl-Lys modifications in chromatin and other proteins and belong to two major families in humans (Taunton et al., 1996), classical HDACs which include 11 Zn metallohydrolase enzymes and seven sirtuins (Wang et al., 2017), that catalyze NAD-dependent Lys deacetylation (Falkenberg and Johnstone, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The class I HDACs, HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC3 are relatively similar at the amino acid sequence level.
source: The class I HDACs, HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC3 are relatively similar at the amino acid sequence level and show overlapping pharmacological sensitivities to the benzamide class of HDAC inhibitors represented by entinostat (Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge.

claim: Class I HDACs show overlapping pharmacological sensitivities to the benzamide class of HDAC inhibitors represented by entinostat.
source: The class I HDACs, HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC3 are relatively similar at the amino acid sequence level and show overlapping pharmacological sensitivities to the benzamide class of HDAC inhibitors represented by entinostat (Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: HDAC1 and HDAC2 are the most similar HDACs.
source: HDAC1 and HDAC2 (Kelly and Cowley, 2013) are the most similar HDACs and are interchangeably found in a variety of multisubunit protein complexes including CoREST, Sin3(A/B), NuRD, and MiDAC whereas HDAC3 is commonly associated with the SMRT/NCoR complex (Bantscheff et al., 2011; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: HDAC1 and HDAC2 are interchangeably found in a variety of multisubunit protein complexes including CoREST, Sin3(A/B), NuRD, and MiDAC.
source: HDAC1 and HDAC2 (Kelly and Cowley, 2013) are the most similar HDACs and are interchangeably found in a variety of multisubunit protein complexes including CoREST, Sin3(A/B), NuRD, and MiDAC whereas HDAC3 is commonly associated with the SMRT/NCoR complex (Bantscheff et al., 2011; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: HDAC3 is commonly associated with the SMRT/NCoR complex.
source: HDAC1 and HDAC2 (Kelly and Cowley, 2013) are the most similar HDACs and are interchangeably found in a variety of multisubunit protein complexes including CoREST, Sin3(A/B), NuRD, and MiDAC whereas HDAC3 is commonly associated with the SMRT/NCoR complex (Bantscheff et al., 2011; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: The CoREST, Sin3, NuRD, and SMRT complexes are generally believed to be involved in silencing of gene expression.
source: The CoREST (Humphrey et al., 2001), Sin3 (Laherty et al., 1997), NuRD (Xue et al., 1998), (Zhang et al., 1999), and SMRT (Guenther et al., 2000), (Wen et al., 2000), (Li et al., 2000) complexes are generally believed to be involved in silencing of gene expression and are recruited by various transcription factors to chromatin in a cell type and cell state dependent manner (Ooi and Wood, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: CoREST, Sin3, NuRD, and SMRT complexes are recruited by various transcription factors to chromatin in a cell type and cell state dependent manner.
source: The CoREST (Humphrey et al., 2001), Sin3 (Laherty et al., 1997), NuRD (Xue et al., 1998), (Zhang et al., 1999), and SMRT (Guenther et al., 2000), (Wen et al., 2000), (Li et al., 2000) complexes are generally believed to be involved in silencing of gene expression and are recruited by various transcription factors to chromatin in a cell type and cell state dependent manner (Ooi and Wood, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The MiDAC complex has been associated with mitotic processes.
source: Less is known about the MiDAC complex although it has been associated with mitotic processes (Bantscheff et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Recent structural studies on each of the five HDAC complexes have provided insights into their distinct molecular architectures.
source: Recent structural studies on each of these five HDAC complexes have provided insights into their distinct molecular architectures (Millard et al., 2017) (CoREST (Song et al., 2020), NuRD (Millard et al., 2016), Sin3A (Clark et al., 2015), MiDAC (Itoh et al., 2015), and SMRT (Watson et al., 2012a) and inositol phosphates have been shown to have varying roles in regulating their stabilities and catalytic activities (Millard et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published structural studies.

claim: Inositol phosphates have been shown to have varying roles in regulating HDAC complex stabilities and catalytic activities.
source: Recent structural studies on each of these five HDAC complexes have provided insights into their distinct molecular architectures (Millard et al., 2017) (CoREST (Song et al., 2020), NuRD (Millard et al., 2016), Sin3A (Clark et al., 2015), MiDAC (Itoh et al., 2015), and SMRT (Watson et al., 2012a) and inositol phosphates have been shown to have varying roles in regulating their stabilities and catalytic activities (Millard et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Histone substrate site-selectivity experiments with HDAC enzymes have generally involved analyzing the isolated HDAC polypeptides or catalytic domains and acetyl-Lys containing histone peptide tails rather than the more physiological HDAC complexes and nucleosome substrates.
source: Histone substrate site-selectivity experiments with HDAC enzymes have generally involved analyzing the isolated HDAC polypeptides or catalytic domains and acetyl-Lys containing histone peptide tails rather than the more physiological HDAC complexes and nucleosome substrates (Zhang et al., 2016), (Riester et al., 2007), (Gurard-Levin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Studies with isolated HDACs and histone peptide substrates have typically shown little to no amino acid sequence site-selectivities for HDACs.
source: Such studies have typically shown little to no amino acid sequence site-selectivities for HDACs.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited literature and represents a summary of previous findings.

claim: The physiological enzyme forms of HDAC1-3 exist in multisubunit complexes.
source: As the physiological enzyme forms of HDAC1-3 exist in multisubunit complexes (Millard et al., 2017) and the natural substrates are chromatin comprised of nucleosomes, histone octamers wrapped by 146 bp of double stranded DNA, the biological relevance of the free HDAC and histone tail substrate peptide experiments is unclear.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The natural substrates of HDACs are chromatin comprised of nucleosomes, histone octamers wrapped by 146 bp of double stranded DNA.
source: As the physiological enzyme forms of HDAC1-3 exist in multisubunit complexes (Millard et al., 2017) and the natural substrates are chromatin comprised of nucleosomes, histone octamers wrapped by 146 bp of double stranded DNA, the biological relevance of the free HDAC and histone tail substrate peptide experiments is unclear.
evidence: This is established knowledge in chromatin biology.

claim: The biological relevance of free HDAC and histone tail substrate peptide experiments is unclear.
source: As the physiological enzyme forms of HDAC1-3 exist in multisubunit complexes (Millard et al., 2017) and the natural substrates are chromatin comprised of nucleosomes, histone octamers wrapped by 146 bp of double stranded DNA, the biological relevance of the free HDAC and histone tail substrate peptide experiments is unclear.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mismatch between experimental systems and physiological conditions.

claim: The CoREST complex includes the enzyme LSD1 which specifically demethylates methyl-Lys4 in histone H3.
source: This was especially interesting because the CoREST complex also includes the enzyme LSD1 which specifically demethylates methyl-Lys4 in histone H3 and this activity is strongly inhibited when the H3 tail also contains acetyl-Lys14 but not acetyl-Lys9 (Kalin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: LSD1 demethylase activity is strongly inhibited when the H3 tail contains acetyl-Lys14 but not acetyl-Lys9.
source: This was especially interesting because the CoREST complex also includes the enzyme LSD1 which specifically demethylates methyl-Lys4 in histone H3 and this activity is strongly inhibited when the H3 tail also contains acetyl-Lys14 but not acetyl-Lys9 (Kalin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Histone H3 marked by Lys14 acetylation and Lys4 methylation may be protected against CoREST complex silencing.
source: These properties suggest a biological role in histone H3 marked by Lys14 acetylation and Lys4 methylation to protect against CoREST complex silencing.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the enzymatic properties described.

claim: Different HDAC complexes may show distinct deacetylase kinetics and nucleosome site selectivities.
source: The CoREST complex enzymatic studies also raise the possibility that different HDAC complexes may show distinct deacetylase kinetics and nucleosome site selectivities.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that the study aims to test.

claim: The kinetics of the HDAC complexes across the range of free acetylated histone H3 substrates are fairly similar.
source: We find that the kinetics of the HDAC complexes across the range of free acetylated histone H3 substrates are fairly similar, whereas there are large differences between the complexes with respect to deacetylase rates and site-selectivity with nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data in Table 1.

claim: There are large differences between the HDAC complexes with respect to deacetylase rates and site-selectivity with nucleosome substrates.
source: We find that the kinetics of the HDAC complexes across the range of free acetylated histone H3 substrates are fairly similar, whereas there are large differences between the complexes with respect to deacetylase rates and site-selectivity with nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: The CoREST complex shows a special resistance to H3K14ac which is largely driven by the preceding Gly13 residue.
source: Among these complexes, the CoREST complex shows a special resistance to H3K14ac which we find is largely driven by the preceding Gly13 residue.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from mutant nucleosome studies.

claim: Semisynthetic X. laevis histone H3 proteins mono-acetylated at positions Lys9, Lys14, Lys18, Lys23, and Lys27 were prepared using F40 sortase.
source: Semisynthetic X. laevis histone H3 proteins (Wang et al., 2015) mono-acetylated at positions Lys9, Lys14, Lys18, Lys23, and Lys27 were prepared using F40 sortase (Piotukh et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: F40 sortase treatment catalyzes transpeptidation leading to ligation of H3 peptide and H3 globular domain fragments to produce pure, scarless full-length modified histone H3s.
source: F40 sortase treatment of the H3 peptide and H3 globular domain catalyzes transpeptidation leading to ligation of the fragments to produce pure, scarless full-length modified histone H3s (Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology, supported by figures showing the results.

claim: Western blot analysis with site-specific acetyl-Lys antibodies demonstrated that each of the semisynthetic histone H3s contained the designated marks.
source: Western blot analysis with the site-specific relevant acetyl-Lys antibodies demonstrated that each of the semisynthetic histone H3s contained the designated marks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The semisynthetic acetylated H3s were incorporated into mononucleosomes containing 146 bp DNA 601 Widom sequence.
source: The semisynthetic acetylated H3s were incorporated into mononucleosomes containing 146 bp DNA 601 Widom sequence (Luger et al., 1997; Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology, supported by citation and figures.

claim: The five HDAC complexes displayed robust catalytic activities with isolated acetylated H3 substrates with velocities (V/E) averaging in the range of 0.5–2 min−1.
source: The five HDAC complexes displayed robust catalytic activities with isolated acetylated H3 substrates with velocities (V/E) averaging in the range of 0.5–2 min−1 and modest differences (largely <3 fold) in acetyl-Lys site-selectivity among K9ac, K14ac, K18ac, K23ac, and K27ac.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 1.

claim: The five HDAC complexes showed modest differences (largely <3 fold) in acetyl-Lys site-selectivity among K9ac, K14ac, K18ac, K23ac, and K27ac with isolated H3 substrates.
source: The five HDAC complexes displayed robust catalytic activities with isolated acetylated H3 substrates with velocities (V/E) averaging in the range of 0.5–2 min−1 and modest differences (largely <3 fold) in acetyl-Lys site-selectivity among K9ac, K14ac, K18ac, K23ac, and K27ac.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 1.

claim: HDAC complexes show similar deacetylase activities as the isolated commercial HDAC1 with free histone H3 substrates.
source: These HDAC complexes show similar deacetylase activities as the isolated commercial HDAC1 (averaging ~0.8 min−1) with free histone H3 substrates.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing HDAC complexes to isolated HDAC1.

claim: Local amino acid context within peptide substrates does not have a large impact on HDAC-catalyzed deacetylation kinetics.
source: These results are generally consistent with the prior studies that have indicated that local amino acid context within peptide substrates does not have a large impact on HDAC-catalyzed deacetylation kinetics (Table 1, Figure 4—figure supplements 1–6A–E,G).
evidence: This is an inference based on the current data and consistency with prior studies.

claim: The HDAC complex velocities (V/E) with acetylated nucleosomes varied over 200-fold, ranging from <0.005 min−1 to 1.2 min−1.
source: The HDAC complex velocities (V/E) with acetylated nucleosomes varied over 200-fold, ranging from <0.005 min−1 to 1.2 min−1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: The MiDAC complex showed the fastest velocities with V/E up to 1.2 min−1 with acetylated nucleosomes.
source: The MiDAC complex showed the fastest velocities with V/E up to 1.2 min−1 whereas the NuRD and Sin3B complexes showed V/E ~ 0.007 min−1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2 and Figure 4.

claim: The NuRD and Sin3B complexes showed V/E ~ 0.007 min−1 with acetylated nucleosomes.
source: The MiDAC complex showed the fastest velocities with V/E up to 1.2 min−1 whereas the NuRD and Sin3B complexes showed V/E ~ 0.007 min−1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: The CoREST and SMRT complexes were intermediate with V/E values averaging in the range of 0.03–0.1 min−1 with acetylated nucleosomes.
source: The CoREST and SMRT complexes were intermediate with V/E values averaging in the range of 0.03–0.1 min−1 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2 and Figure 3.

claim: CoREST showed similar velocities (V/E 0.06–0.1 min−1) for K9ac, K18ac, K23ac, and K27ac that were markedly greater than the V/E for K14ac (<0.005 min−1) with nucleosome substrates.
source: CoREST showed similar velocities (V/E 0.06–0.1 min−1) for K9ac, K18ac, K23ac, and K27ac that were markedly greater than the V/E for K14ac (<0.005 min−1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: The MiDAC complex velocity for deacetylating K9ac (V/E 1.2 min−1) was only about 2-fold greater than for K14ac (V/E 0.52 min−1) with nucleosome substrates.
source: In contrast, the MiDAC complex velocity for deacetylating K9ac (V/E 1.2 min−1) was only about 2-fold greater than for K14ac (V/E 0.52 min−1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2 and Figure 4.

claim: The MiDAC complex deacetylated K23ac at a much lower rate (V/E 0.048 min−1) relative to K9ac removal.
source: However, the MiDAC complex deacetylated K23ac at a much lower rate (V/E 0.048 min−1) relative to K9ac removal and in general, MiDAC deacetylase activity decreased when comparing more C-terminal acetyl-Lys sites in H3 with more N-terminal locations (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2 and Figure 4.

claim: MiDAC deacetylase activity decreased when comparing more C-terminal acetyl-Lys sites in H3 with more N-terminal locations.
source: However, the MiDAC complex deacetylated K23ac at a much lower rate (V/E 0.048 min−1) relative to K9ac removal and in general, MiDAC deacetylase activity decreased when comparing more C-terminal acetyl-Lys sites in H3 with more N-terminal locations (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The SMRT complex showed the highest rates of deacetylase activities on K9ac and K27ac.
source: The one HDAC3 complex investigated here, SMRT, showed the highest rates of deacetylase activities on K9ac and K27ac and in general had more similar rates across the five sites compared with CoREST and MiDAC.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: SMRT had more similar rates across the five acetylation sites compared with CoREST and MiDAC.
source: The one HDAC3 complex investigated here, SMRT, showed the highest rates of deacetylase activities on K9ac and K27ac and in general had more similar rates across the five sites compared with CoREST and MiDAC.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: NuRD and Sin3B displayed very low similar deacetylase activity at every H3 acetyl-Lys site.
source: The activities of NuRD and Sin3B displayed very low similar deacetylase activity at every H3 acetyl-Lys site (Table 2, Figure 4—figure supplements 1–6A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2 and supplementary figures.

claim: K9acR8G nucleosomes displayed a ~ 3 fold deacetylase rate reduction compared with WT K9ac when treated with the CoREST complex.
source: The K9acR8G nucleosomes displayed a ~ 3 fold deacetylase rate reduction compared with WT K9ac (K9acR8G V/E 0.029 min−1 vs WT K9ac V/E 0.1 min−1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: K14acG13R nucleosomes showed a > 17 fold increase in deacetylase rate vs. WT K14ac when treated with the CoREST complex.
source: Remarkably, K14acG13R nucleosomes showed a > 17 fold increase in deacetylase rate vs. WT K14ac (K14acG13R V/E 0.084 min−1 vs. WT K14ac V/E < 0.005 min−1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The near matching of V/E deacetylase values of the CoREST complex on K14acG13R and WT K9ac nucleosomes suggests a profound rejection of a Gly at the H3 13th position in nucleosomes by the CoREST complex.
source: The near matching of V/E deacetylase values of the CoREST complex on K14acG13R and WT K9ac nucleosomes suggests a profound rejection of a Gly at the H3 13th position in nucleosomes by the CoREST complex although it is more tolerated at the 8 position of H3.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, representing an inference from the results.

claim: Gly at the H3 13th position is more tolerated at the 8 position of H3 by the CoREST complex.
source: The near matching of V/E deacetylase values of the CoREST complex on K14acG13R and WT K9ac nucleosomes suggests a profound rejection of a Gly at the H3 13th position in nucleosomes by the CoREST complex although it is more tolerated at the 8 position of H3.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of mutant and wild-type nucleosome deacetylation rates.

claim: K9acR8G nucleosome deacetylation by the MiDAC complex matched that of WT K9ac nucleosomes (V/E 1.2 min−1 for both).
source: In fact, K9acR8G nucleosome deacetylation by the MiDAC complex matched that of WT K9ac nucleosomes (V/E 1.2 min−1 for both).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: K14acG13R nucleosome deacetylation by MiDAC was accelerated by 2.5 fold relative to WT K14ac nucleosomes.
source: K14acG13R nucleosome deacetylation by MiDAC was accelerated by 2.5 fold relative to WT K14ac nuclesomes, indicating a minor preference for Arg at the H3 13th position.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: MiDAC shows a minor preference for Arg at the H3 13th position.
source: K14acG13R nucleosome deacetylation by MiDAC was accelerated by 2.5 fold relative to WT K14ac nuclesomes, indicating a minor preference for Arg at the H3 13th position.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The deacetylation rate (V/E) for NuRD on H4K16ac nucleosomes was low and similar to those of the acetylated H3 nucleosomes.
source: However, the deacetylation rate (V/E) for NuRD was low and similar to those of the acetylated H3 nucleosomes (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The low nucleosome deacetylase activity of RBBP4-containing HDAC complexes may be unrelated to RBBP4/H3 interaction.
source: These results suggest that the low nucleosome deacetylase activity of RBBP4-containing HDAC complexes may be unrelated to RBBP4/H3 interaction.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the H4K16ac nucleosome data.

claim: Distinct HDAC1 complexes can show sharply different deacetylase activities toward different nucleosome substrates.
source: A principal finding of this study is that distinct HDAC1 complexes can show sharply different deacetylase activities toward different nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data.

claim: The unique biological consequences of the various HDAC1 complexes are not simply dependent on where they are recruited to in chromatin and by which particular transcription factor.
source: This would appear to suggest that the unique biological consequences of the various HDAC1 complexes are not simply dependent on where they are recruited to in chromatin and by which particular transcription factor (Watson et al., 2012b).
evidence: This is an inference based on the finding of different catalytic properties among complexes.

claim: The different catalytic properties and site-selectivities of the HDAC1 complexes likely drive different patterns of histone deacetylation and chromatin states.
source: Rather, the different catalytic properties and site-selectivities of the HDAC1 complexes likely drive different patterns of histone deacetylation and chromatin states.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: HDAC1 and HDAC2 have very high sequence homology.
source: Furthermore, because HDAC1 and HDAC2 have very high sequence homology, we believe it is likely that HDAC1 and HDAC2 will behave in similar ways in terms of the nucleosome deacetylation assays carried out here.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: HDAC1 and HDAC2 will likely behave in similar ways in terms of nucleosome deacetylation assays.
source: Furthermore, because HDAC1 and HDAC2 have very high sequence homology, we believe it is likely that HDAC1 and HDAC2 will behave in similar ways in terms of the nucleosome deacetylation assays carried out here.
evidence: This is a speculation based on sequence homology.

claim: K14ac blocks the removal of H3K4 methylation by the CoREST complex.
source: It is likely not a coincidence that K14ac blocks the removal of H3K4 methylation as this could allow doubly modified H3K4me1/2 and H3K14ac tails to be immune from the silencing action of the CoREST complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enzymatic properties described and cited literature.

claim: Doubly modified H3K4me1/2 and H3K14ac tails could be immune from the silencing action of the CoREST complex.
source: It is likely not a coincidence that K14ac blocks the removal of H3K4 methylation as this could allow doubly modified H3K4me1/2 and H3K14ac tails to be immune from the silencing action of the CoREST complex.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the enzymatic data.

claim: H3K4 methylation is commonly found in the context of enhancer elements in DNA.
source: H3K4 methylation is known to be commonly found in the context of enhancer elements in DNA (Hsu et al., 2018), which is also associated with H3K14ac (Karmodiya et al., 2012), possibly insulating such K4 methylation by CoREST.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: H3K14ac is associated with enhancer elements in DNA.
source: H3K4 methylation is known to be commonly found in the context of enhancer elements in DNA (Hsu et al., 2018), which is also associated with H3K14ac (Karmodiya et al., 2012), possibly insulating such K4 methylation by CoREST.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: H3K14ac may insulate H3K4 methylation from CoREST action.
source: H3K4 methylation is known to be commonly found in the context of enhancer elements in DNA (Hsu et al., 2018), which is also associated with H3K14ac (Karmodiya et al., 2012), possibly insulating such K4 methylation by CoREST.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the enzymatic properties and genomic context.

claim: The presence of Gly13 rather than an Arg residue is a principal determinant of the meager rate of CoREST-mediated deacetylation of K14ac in nucleosome substrates.
source: The Gly/Arg swaps at positions 8 and 13 in histone H3 clearly demonstrate that the presence of Gly13 rather than an Arg residue is a principal determinant of the meager rate of CoREST-mediated deacetylation of K14ac in nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by the mutant nucleosome experimental data.

claim: Each of the five class I HDAC complexes examined were relatively ineffective at deacetylating K14ac in the context of nucleosomes presumably at least partly due to Gly13.
source: However, each of the five class I HDAC complexes examined here were relatively ineffective at deacetylating K14ac in the context of nucleosomes presumably at least partly due to Gly13.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: The molecular recognition of Lys14ac by HDAC complexes is altered when the H3 tail is presented to the HDAC1 active site in a chromatin context.
source: That this K14ac deselection is not true in isolated H3 indicates that the molecular recognition of Lys14ac by these HDAC complexes is altered when the H3 tail is presented to the HDAC1 active site in a chromatin context.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of isolated H3 and nucleosome substrate data.

claim: H3K14ac is a relatively abundant mark at baseline.
source: The cellular relevance of these findings is supported by the fact that H3K14ac is a relatively abundant mark at baseline (Sidoli and Garcia, 2017) and is rather unaffected by class I HDAC inhibitor treatment compared with H3K9ac and H3K27ac which show substantial increases with such inhibitors (Schölz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: H3K14ac is rather unaffected by class I HDAC inhibitor treatment compared with H3K9ac and H3K27ac which show substantial increases with such inhibitors.
source: The cellular relevance of these findings is supported by the fact that H3K14ac is a relatively abundant mark at baseline (Sidoli and Garcia, 2017) and is rather unaffected by class I HDAC inhibitor treatment compared with H3K9ac and H3K27ac which show substantial increases with such inhibitors (Schölz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Robust histone acetyltransferase targeting H3K14 may contribute to the elevated H3K14 acetylation levels in cells.
source: It is also possible that robust histone acetyltransferase targeting H3K14 contributes to the elevated H3K14 acetylation levels in cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cellular data.

claim: The MiDAC complex showed the speediest average deacetylation rate across the five acetyl-Lys marks in nucleosomes.
source: The MiDAC complex showed far and away the speediest average deacetylation rate across the five acetyl-Lys marks looked at in nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: MiDAC deacetylated K9ac nucleosomes (V/E 1.2 min−1) more rapidly than K9ac in free H3 histones.
source: Impressively, MiDAC deacetylated K9ac nucleosomes (V/E 1.2 min−1) more rapidly than K9ac in free H3 histones.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data comparing nucleosome and free histone substrates.

claim: MiDAC is not known to be recruited to chromatin by transcription factors like CoREST, NuRD, Sin3B, and SMRT.
source: Unlike CoREST, NuRD, Sin3B, and SMRT which are thought to be transcriptional silencers and recruited to chromatin by transcription factors, MiDAC is not known to be employed in this way.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about MiDAC function.

claim: MiDAC's ground state affinity to chromatin is thought to be quite high.
source: Furthermore, its ground state affinity to chromatin is thought to be quite high (Itoh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: There was a modest trend for the rate of MiDAC deacetylation to be highest closest to the N-terminus of H3 in the context of nucleosome substrates.
source: It is interesting that there was a modest trend for the rate of deacetylation to be highest closest to the N-terminus of H3 in the context of nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is an observation based on the experimental data.

claim: The extreme N-terminus of the H3 tail in chromatin may have greater accessibility to the HDAC1 active site in the MiDAC complex.
source: We speculate that this may represent a greater accessibility of the extreme N-terminus of the H3 tail in chromatin to the HDAC1 active site in this complex.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the positional trend in deacetylation rates.

claim: The NuRD and Sin3B complexes showed the lowest deacetylation rates with H3 acetylated nucleosomes.
source: In contrast to MiDAC, the NuRD and Sin3B complexes showed the lowest deacetylation rates with H3 acetylated nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Table 2.

claim: NuRD and Sin3B may have a more extreme requirement for recruitment to nucleosomes by a transcription factor compared with the other HDAC complexes.
source: It is plausible the NuRD and Sin3B may have a more extreme requirement for recruitment to nucleosomes by a transcription factor compared with the other HDAC complexes looked at here (Zhang et al., 2018), (Walsh, 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: There could be an additional macromolecular component or post-translational modification lacking in the experimental system that would unleash the deacetylase activity or alter substrate selectivities of HDAC complexes on nucleosomes.
source: In addition, there could be an additional macromolecular component or post-translational modification (Wang, 2019) lacking in our system that would unleash the deacetylase activity or alter substrate selectivities of any of the HDAC complexes on nucleosomes (Hudson et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: NuRD and other HDAC complexes have been reported to have a variety of additional protein subunits depending on cell type and cell state.
source: Indeed, NuRD and the other HDAC complexes investigated here have been reported to have a variety of additional protein subunits depending on cell type and cell state (Millard et al., 2016), (Lai and Wade, 2011), (Yang and Seto, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The chromatin remodelling module of NuRD is rather loosely associated.
source: For the NuRD complex, however, it is established that the chromatin remodelling module is rather loosely associated, and we do not expect that its absence would greatly influence HDAC activity.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about NuRD complex structure.

claim: The absence of the chromatin remodelling module would not greatly influence NuRD HDAC activity.
source: For the NuRD complex, however, it is established that the chromatin remodelling module is rather loosely associated, and we do not expect that its absence would greatly influence HDAC activity.
evidence: This is a speculation based on structural knowledge.

claim: The NuRD or Sin3B complexes could show very high site-selectivity on one or more sites in histones beyond the acetylated-Lys examined in H3 or H4.
source: In addition to roles for transcription factors and additional subunits, the NuRD or Sin3B complexes could show very high site-selectivity on one or more sites in histones beyond the acetylated-Lys that we have examined thus far in H3 or H4.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation suggesting future research directions.

claim: NAD-dependent sirtuins may also show site-selectivities.
source: We have focused on classical HDAC acetyl-Lys selectivities in chromatin. However, there is reason to believe that the NAD-dependent sirtuins may also show site-selectivities.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings with classical HDACs.

claim: Sirt7 shows a strong preference for H3K36ac in the context of chromatin.
source: Recent studies on Sirt7 have shown that this enzyme shows a strong preference for H3K36ac in the context of chromatin (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.
